NM-2026-SM7.title: REDISTRICTING TASK FORCE

actions.text: Sent to Senate Rules Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee

NM-2026-SM7.aiSummary: This memorial would ask the New Mexico Legislative Council to form a redistricting task force to study ways to improve how district maps are drawn. The task force would look at changes to the state's redistricting law, how other states do it, and other possible reforms. It would include lawmakers, party leaders, and members of the public, and it would present its findings and ideas by December 31, 2027.

NM-2026-SM26.title: UTILITIES IN REGIONAL TRANSMISSION ORGS.
NM-2026-SM26.policyArea: MEMORIALS, OTHER, UTILITIES (sewer, electric, gas, water, telephone)
NM-2026-SM26.aiSummary: This memorial would ask the New Mexico Senate to support utilities joining regional power markets, including voluntary energy markets. It says this could help coordinate electric service across states, improve reliability, and keep power more affordable for residents. It also calls for oversight by the Public Regulation Commission and sends copies to state leaders and agencies.

NM-2026-SB313.title: CHILD CAR SEAT FASTENING AS NEGLIGENCE

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Tax, Business and Transportation Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee

NM-2026-SB313.policyArea: CHILDREN & FAMILIES, MOTOR VEHICLES (autos, trucks, buses, cycles)
NM-2026-SB313.aiSummary: The bill would let a court treat a child's failure to use a car seat, booster seat, or seat belt as fault or negligence in a crash case. It would remove the current rule that such a failure cannot reduce or split damages. This would affect children riding in passenger cars, vans, and pickup trucks, and the people involved in injury claims after a crash.

NM-2026-SB250.title: IGNITION INTERLOCK FOR REVOKED LICENSE

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Tax, Business and Transportation Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee

NM-2026-SB250.policyArea: ALCOHOL & DRUGS, CRIMES & PENALTIES, MOTOR VEHICLES (autos, trucks, buses, cycles)
NM-2026-SB250.aiSummary: This bill would require people convicted of driving on a revoked license to get an ignition interlock device, which is a breath test linked to a car, and to get an ignition interlock license within 10 days. It would also make that offense a court-of-record case in metropolitan court, set ignition interlock licenses at 4 or 8 years, and let an approved installer remove the device without a court order. The bill would also change the interlock device fund rules and raise some payment limits for device costs.

NM-2026-SB246.title: MASSAGE THERAPY PRACTICE CHANGES

actions.text: Sent to House Health & Human Services Committee
DO PASS, as amended, committee report adopted
Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Health and Public Affairs Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee

NM-2026-SB246.aiSummary: The bill would add licensing rules for massage therapy businesses and define a massage therapy establishment as a place where massage therapy is offered or done. It would let the board set standards, inspect these places, and fine or discipline people who run or work in an unlicensed place. It would also require new or renewed massage therapy licenses or registrations issued on or after July 1, 2026 to include a current photo.

NM-2026-SB228.title: GENERAL APPROPRIATION ACT OF 2026

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB228.policyArea: FINANCE, PUBLIC, STATE AGENCIES & DEPARTMENTS (including reorganization)
NM-2026-SB228.aiSummary: The bill would set the state budget for fiscal year 2027 and give money to state agencies, courts, and other parts of state government. It also sets rules for how the money would be spent, including when unused funds must return to the general fund. The bill covers many agencies and programs, including the legislative, judicial, and district courts.

NM-2026-SB219.title: NATIVE AMERICAN OMBUD ACT

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Indian, Rural and Cultural Affairs Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB219.aiSummary: The bill would create a new state office to help Native Americans in New Mexico by looking into concerns, trying to resolve them, and reporting on common problems. It would require people who serve Native Americans to post notice about the office, keep its records private, and bar retaliation against anyone who brings a concern. The bill would set aside $2 million from the general fund for the office and say it would take effect right away.

NM-2026-SB106.title: GRADUATE SCHOLARSHIP ACT FUNDING

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Education Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB106.aiSummary: The bill would give $5 million from the general fund to the Higher Education Department for fiscal year 2027 to carry out the Graduate Scholarship Act. It would affect the department and the graduate scholarship program it runs.

NM-2026-HB107.title: MEDICAL MALPRACTICE CLAIM CHANGES

actions.text: not printed House Rules and Order of Business Committee

NM-2026-HB107.aiSummary: The bill would change New Mexico's medical malpractice law, including some legal definitions and how claims are paid. It would lower a health care provider's personal liability limit to $200,000, keep limits on total damage awards in malpractice cases, and make payments from the patient's compensation fund as expenses are actually incurred. It would also limit punitive damages and attorney fees in malpractice claims.
